If your horse used to drive hard from behind and now he's just… coasting, that's not fitness. That's not age. That's worth checking.

Horse's that lose hind-end push are often locked through the pelvis and lower back. The joints stop moving freely, and the power doesn't get transferred forward. What looks like a lazy stop or a weak rate is actually a horse working around something that hurts.

Dr. Leo sees this pattern across the performance horses he works in North Texas — ropers, barrel horses, cutters. Different disciplines, same locked-up hips.

You can keep drilling the rate. Or you can find out why it disappeared.
